body:
## Summary
The Review page's feedback state is an optimistic overlay with one rollback snapshot per call and one shared pending flag. Make it a per-line sequenced write ledger (draft -> sending#seq -> saved | failed(payload)) so a late failure never clobbers a newer success, pending is per line, the player can advance before the daemon answers, and a failed mark is retryable instead of a transient status string.

## Description
hooks.ts:38-51 snapshots `before` and restores it on any failure, so two writes to one line resolve last-to-fail-wins rather than last-written-wins. useMutation's pending is one boolean per hook (data/react.tsx:90-97), so Save is disabled on every line while any line saves, and the keyboard path (Player.tsx:102) is not guarded at all. The overlay is never pruned (hooks.ts:28) and review.session is never refetched for feedback (invalidation.ts:29), so the overlay silently outranks any later server state. A pure `ledger.ts` reducer keyed by line holds entries {seq, payload, state}; a reply settles only the entry whose seq it carries; a failure reverts to the newest acknowledged state for that line, not a snapshot; a server row at or after the ack prunes the entry. Leans on review-iteration-loops / gate-record-outlives-the-media: the operator's judgement is attention spent once, so its record must never be silently lost or shown wrong - the record is a queue whose rows carry whether they landed.

## Flow
- ledger.ts: reducer + selectors (byLine, statusOf(line), failed()) - pure, unit tested first
- hooks.ts: useFeedback drives the ledger; save() enqueues and returns a seq; per-line pending
- FeedbackPanel: disabled/status from statusOf(line), not set.pending or a string
- Player: Save and next advances on enqueue; PlayerParts shows a failed-marks notice with Retry
- Moment: the drawer's panel shows the same per-line status

## Expected impact
No mark ever displays a state the daemon does not hold; the player's step time stops including the daemon's append round trip; a failed write is recoverable from the screen instead of a status line that vanishes on the next line.

## Evaluation
Claim: concurrent and failed feedback writes resolve to the newest write, per line, and the player does not block on the RPC.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (cases 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 fail on today's code by the cited lines; case 2 has no per-line status to assert)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first (ledger.test.ts pure; player.test.tsx with a held review.feedback.set double)
Result: better
Gate: architecture

body:
## Summary
The operator runs a sandbox session, changes the brain, runs another, and today has to judge 'better or worse' by flipping between two session pages and remembering numbers. Add a compare view, `review/<A>/compare/<B>`, reached in one click from any session ('Compare with previous'), that answers the iteration question directly: rules newly failing / fixed / still failing, gate checks that flipped, reply-wait and silence figures with deltas against the page's limits, line-mix share shifts and quality-dimension moves.

## Description
The page already holds every number needed, per session: verdict rules and evidence, checks, derive()'s replyWaitS and mix, dimRows. It never sets two side by side - the wall only sorts (Layer1.tsx:67-72) and every tab is one session (Layer2.tsx:27). A pure `compare.ts` takes two (ReviewSession, Derived) pairs and returns the diff; Compare.tsx renders it with the existing Section/Chip/StatBand primitives. Leans on review-iteration-loops: review exists to drive the next revision, and its unmeasured-is-not-pass law (stale certificates failure mode) sets the rule that an unjudged side shows as unmeasured, never as a clean pass.

## Flow
- compare.ts: ruleDiff, checkDiff, figureDiff (with limit crossings), mixDiff, dimDiff - pure, tested first
- tab.ts / Layer2.tsx: TabId 'compare', known-check accepts a session-id arg, tab bar gains 'Compare with previous' (from useSessions by started_ms)
- index.ts: breadcrumb label 'Compare'
- Compare.tsx (+ minimal css): two useSession reads, five sections, rule refs open the owning session's timeline line

## Expected impact
The operator's after-change question ('did that fix it, and what did it break?') becomes one click and one screen instead of two pages and memory; regressions hidden behind an unchanged pass/fail verdict (one rule swapping for another, reply p95 drifting over 4 s) become visible.

## Evaluation
Claim: two sessions can be compared on rules, checks, figures, mix and quality from one route.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no compare route or diff exists)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first (compare.test.tsx: pure diff cases on tabs.fixture sessions plus a mounted Layer2 route test)
Result: better
Gate: direction (new in-scope review mode); review.l2 css budget checked by `pnpm -C apps/console build`
